name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_OF_RADIATION_AND_MATTER_MCQ_Q01 - Chronological order of early atomic discoveries

questiontext.text:
The following historical discoveries provided foundational milestones leading to the modern understanding of atomic structure and the dual nature of radiation and matter:

  1. Discovery of cathode rays by William Crookes
  2. Discovery of X-rays by Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen
  3. Experimental determination of specific charge \((e/m)\) and naming of the electron by J. J. Thomson
  4. Pioneering oil-drop experiment establishing the quantization of electric charge by R. A. Millikan

Which of the following represents the correct chronological sequence of these scientific milestones?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical Identification of Discovery Dates
The historical milestones described in the textbook occurred as follows:

  • William Crookes discovered cathode rays in 1870, later suggesting in 1879 that they consist of streams of fast-moving negatively charged particles.
  • Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 during experimental investigations of electric discharge through gases at low pressure.
  • J. J. Thomson experimentally determined the speed and specific charge \((e/m = 1.76 \times 10^{11}\text{ C/kg})\) of cathode ray particles in 1897 and named them electrons.
  • R. A. Millikan performed the oil-drop experiment in 1913, demonstrating that electric charge is quantised in integral multiples of \(1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
Arranging these discoveries according to their calendar years: \[ 1870 \text{ (Crookes)} \longrightarrow 1895 \text{ (Roentgen)} \longrightarrow 1897 \text{ (Thomson)} \longrightarrow 1913 \text{ (Millikan)} \]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological order of the milestones is I → II → III → IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_OF_RADIATION_AND_MATTER_MCQ_Q02 - Chronological sequence of quantum radiation milestones

questiontext.text:
Consider the following landmark events in the development of the quantum picture of radiation and the concept of matter waves:

  1. Proposal of light quanta (\(E = h\nu\)) by Albert Einstein to explain the photoelectric effect
  2. Experimental verification of Einstein's photoelectric equation and determination of Planck's constant by R. A. Millikan
  3. Award of the Nobel Prize in Physics to Albert Einstein for his contributions to theoretical physics and the photoelectric effect
  4. Proposal of the matter wave hypothesis (\(\lambda = h/p\)) by Louis Victor de Broglie

Which of the following represents the correct chronological sequence of these developments?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical Timeline of Key Quantum Milestones
Reviewing the recorded dates for each achievement as documented in the chapter:

  • Albert Einstein proposed the radically new picture of electromagnetic radiation built up of discrete energy quanta (\(E = h\nu\)) to explain the photoelectric effect in 1905.
  • R. A. Millikan conducted systematic experiments on alkali metals between 1906 and 1916, conclusively proving the validity of Einstein's photoelectric equation and determining Planck's constant in 1916.
  • Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his contribution to theoretical physics and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect.
  • Louis Victor de Broglie put forward his revolutionary hypothesis that moving particles of matter display wave-like properties with wavelength \(\lambda = h/p\) in 1924.

Step 2: Chronological Ordering
Arranging these achievements in sequential order of their occurrence: \[ 1905 \text{ (Einstein's hypothesis)} \longrightarrow 1916 \text{ (Millikan's verification)} \longrightarrow 1921 \text{ (Einstein's Nobel Prize)} \longrightarrow 1924 \text{ (de Broglie's matter waves)} \]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct chronological sequence is I → II → III → IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_OF_RADIATION_AND_MATTER_MCQ_Q03 - Sequential stages in photoelectric emission mechanism

questiontext.text:
Consider the following microscopic and circuit processes that take place during the operation of a photoelectric cell when incident radiation of frequency \(\nu > \nu_0\) strikes a photosensitive emitter cathode:

  1. Transmission of incident radiation through the quartz window onto the photosensitive plate
  2. Absorption of a discrete photon of energy \(h\nu\) by an individual conduction electron
  3. Expenditure of energy to overcome the surface work function \(\phi_0\) against the attractive pull of metal ions
  4. Ejection of the photoelectron with kinetic energy up to \(K_{\max} = h\nu - \phi_0\) into the evacuated space
  5. Collection of the photoelectron at the positive anode, establishing an electric current recorded by the microammeter

What is the correct logical and chronological order of these processes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Optical Transmission and Illumination
The process initiates externally when radiation emitted by the source passes through the transparent quartz window of the evacuated tube and illuminates the surface of the photosensitive emitter plate.

Step 2: Quantum Energy Absorption
In accordance with Einstein's quantum picture, radiation energy is concentrated in discrete quanta. When light falls upon the surface, an individual free conduction electron absorbs a single quantum of energy \(h\nu\) instantaneously (within \(\sim 10^{-9}\text{ s}\) or less).

Step 3: Overcoming the Surface Barrier
Before escaping from the metal, the electron must perform work to overcome the attractive electrostatic forces exerted by the positive lattice ions at the metal boundary, expending an energy amount at least equal to the work function \(\phi_0\).

Step 4: Photoelectron Emission
The remaining energy appears as kinetic energy. The most energetic electrons emerge from the surface into the evacuated chamber with maximum kinetic energy given by: \[ K_{\max} = h\nu - \phi_0 \]

Step 5: Transport and Current Measurement
Once in the evacuated tube, the liberated photoelectrons are drawn across the gap by the accelerating electric field maintained between the electrodes. Upon reaching the positive collector plate, they complete the circuit, producing a steady photocurrent detected by the microammeter.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The physical and logical sequence proceeds as: transmission of radiation → photon absorption → overcoming the work function barrier → emission into vacuum → collection and current registration. This corresponds strictly to I → II → III → IV → V.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_OF_RADIATION_AND_MATTER_MCQ_Q04 - Increasing order of particle de Broglie wavelengths

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four moving bodies discussed in the study of matter waves:

  1. An electron of mass \(m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\) moving with a speed of \(5.4 \times 10^{6}\text{ m/s}\)
  2. A proton of mass \(m = 1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\) moving with a speed of \(2.0 \times 10^{4}\text{ m/s}\)
  3. A dust particle of mass \(m = 1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ kg}\) drifting with a speed of \(2.2\text{ m/s}\)
  4. A ball of mass \(m = 0.150\text{ kg}\) travelling with a speed of \(30.0\text{ m/s}\)

Which of the following correctly arranges these bodies in order of increasing de Broglie wavelength?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formula for de Broglie Wavelength
The de Broglie wavelength associated with any material particle of mass \(m\) moving with velocity \(v\) is given by: \[ \lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{m v} \] where Planck's constant is \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Calculation for Each Moving Entity

  • For the electron: \[ p_{\text{electron}} = (9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}) \times (5.4 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}) \approx 4.92 \times 10^{-24}\text{ kg m/s} \] \[ \lambda_{\text{electron}} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{4.92 \times 10^{-24}\text{ kg m/s}} \approx 1.35 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \]
  • For the proton: \[ p_{\text{proton}} = (1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}) \times (2.0 \times 10^4\text{ m/s}) \approx 3.34 \times 10^{-23}\text{ kg m/s} \] \[ \lambda_{\text{proton}} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{3.34 \times 10^{-23}\text{ kg m/s}} \approx 1.99 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} \]
  • For the dust particle: \[ p_{\text{dust}} = (1.0 \times 10^{-9}\text{ kg}) \times (2.2\text{ m/s}) = 2.2 \times 10^{-9}\text{ kg m/s} \] \[ \lambda_{\text{dust}} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{2.2 \times 10^{-9}\text{ kg m/s}} \approx 3.01 \times 10^{-25}\text{ m} \]
  • For the ball: \[ p_{\text{ball}} = (0.150\text{ kg}) \times (30.0\text{ m/s}) = 4.50\text{ kg m/s} \] \[ \lambda_{\text{ball}} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{4.50\text{ kg m/s}} \approx 1.47 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m} \]

Step 3: Comparison and Sequential Ordering
Comparing the calculated matter wavelengths: \[ 1.47 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m} < 3.01 \times 10^{-25}\text{ m} < 1.99 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} < 1.35 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \] Therefore, in increasing order of de Broglie wavelength: \[ \text{Ball} < \text{Dust particle} < \text{Proton} < \text{Electron} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence arranged in order of increasing de Broglie wavelength is IV → III → II → I.
